# Volume 2 — IV Different Opinions

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

As the sun was setting one evening, Odette Pullen, Hugh Carrow, and Nell Harcourt stayed a while beside a fence beneath softly rustling spruce branches, at the junction where a trail through the trees named the Aspen Path met the primary thoroughfare. Having gone up to pass the afternoon hours in Nell's company, Odette was being accompanied a portion of her journey back by Nell; the pair encountered Hugh at the fence, and the three of them were presently conversing regarding the momentous next day; this was because that upcoming day marked the first of September, bringing the commencement of the school term. Stonebridge was where Odette would travel, whereas Pale Sands was Hugh's destination.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0000 }

“The two of you possess an edge over me,” Nell sighed. “Your future pupils do not know you, whereas I am required to instruct my former classmates, and Mrs. Sowerby mentions her fear that they will fail to respect me the way they would a newcomer, unless I act extremely strict right from the start. However, I am not convinced that an educator ought to be strict. Oh, I feel as though this is such an immense duty!”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0001 }

“I guess we’ll get on all right,” Odette stated in a relaxed manner. No desires to act as a positive inspiration bothered Odette. Her intentions were to honestly merit her pay, satisfy the board, and have her name placed on the honor roll of the School Inspector. Beyond these, Odette possessed no other goals. “The main thing will be to keep order and a teacher has to be a little cross to do that. If my pupils won’t do as I tell them I shall punish them.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0002 }

“How?”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0003 }

“Naturally, administer a proper thrashing to them.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0004 }

“Oh, Odette, you would not,” Nell exclaimed, appalled. “Odette, you could not!”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0005 }

“I certainly could and would, provided they merited it,” Odette stated with determination.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0006 }

“I could never strike a youngster,” stated Nell with the same firmness. “I do not support it whatsoever. Miss Thorne never struck a single one of us yet maintained absolute discipline; whereas Mr. Pidgeon was constantly striking and maintained no discipline whatsoever. No, should I be unable to succeed without striking, I will not attempt to instruct a class. Superior methods of discipline exist. I will endeavor to gain my students’ love, which will make them desire to follow my instructions.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0007 }

“However, what if they fail to do so?” inquired pragmatic Odette.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0008 }

“I would not beat them regardless. I am certain that it would not accomplish a thing. Oh, do not beat your students, Odette dear, regardless of their actions.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0009 }

“How do you feel about this, Hugh?” asked Odette. “Is it your belief that certain children truly require a spanking from time to time?”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0010 }

“Is it not your opinion that whipping a youngster . . . any youngster, is a brutal, merciless act?” Nell burst out, her cheeks turning red with intensity.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0011 }

“Well,” Hugh uttered in a deliberate manner, caught between his genuine beliefs and his desire to satisfy Nell’s expectations, “valid arguments exist for each perspective. My belief is not in the frequent spanking of kids. As you mention, Nell, my opinion is that superior methods of discipline generally exist, making physical correction an ultimate measure. However, looking at the opposite view, just as Odette mentions, my conviction is that a rare youngster exists who remains unresponsive to different approaches and who, to put it briefly, requires a spanking and would benefit from one. My principle will be physical correction used solely when all else fails.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0012 }

Attempting to satisfy both parties, Hugh achieved the customary and entirely proper result of satisfying no one. A toss of her head came from Odette.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0013 }

“I’ll give my pupils a whipping whenever they misbehave. That is the most direct and simple method to persuade them.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0014 }

A look of disappointment was cast toward Hugh by Nell.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0015 }

“I will under no circumstances beat a young one,” she reiterated with determination. “I am convinced it is neither proper nor required.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0016 }

“What if a boy gave you attitude when you gave him an order?” Odette asked.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0017 }

“I’d make him stay after class and speak to him with kindness and firmness,” Nell said. “Goodness exists within each individual if you are able to locate it. Finding and cultivating it is the obligation of an educator. As you are aware, that is what we were instructed by our Regent’s School Management professor. Do you think that by beating a child you could discover any goodness in them? Professor Rennie asserts that guiding the children correctly matters much more than even instructing them in the three R’s.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0018 }

“Yet the Inspector tests them in reading, writing, and arithmetic, remember, and he will not present you with a favorable report unless they reach his level,” Odette objected.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0019 }

“I would prefer that my students affectionally regard me and remember me in future years as a genuine benefactor instead of being listed on the honor roll,” Nell firmly declared.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0020 }

“If children were to misbehave, would you refrain from punishing them entirely?” Hugh inquired.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0021 }

“Oh, indeed, I think I must, even though I am certain I will detest doing it. However, you are able to detain them during recess, make them stand on the floor, or assign them lines for writing.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0022 }

“I assume you will not discipline the girls by forcing them to sit beside the boys?” Odette asked cunningly.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0023 }

Hugh and Nell exchanged glances, wearing somewhat silly grins. A long time ago, Nell was forced to sit next to Hugh as a disciplinary measure, and the results of that event had proved gloomy and painful.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0024 }

“Indeed, future events shall demonstrate the superior method,” Odette remarked wisely when the two of them separated.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0025 }

Nell returned to Grey Shutters by travelling along Aspen Path, which was dim, whispering, and fragrant with ferns, through Primrose Dell and past Reedmere, where shade and brightness touched beneath the fir trees, and downward along Linger Lane . . . places that she and Isolde had given those names to a long time before. Moving at an unhurried pace, she took pleasure in the sweet air of the woods and fields as well as the starry summer dusk, while giving serious thought to the unfamiliar responsibilities she would assume the next day. Upon arriving at the yard at Grey Shutters, the booming, firm voice of Mrs. Sowerby drifted outward from the unclosed kitchen window.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0026 }

With a wry face, Nell reflected, “Mrs. Sowerby has arrived to offer me wise counsel regarding tomorrow, but I doubt I will enter. It seems to me that her counsel resembles pepper . . . fine when used sparingly, yet quite fiery when she dispenses it. Rather than that, I will dash across to converse with Mr. Pettifer.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0027 }

Ever since the memorable incident involving the Jersey cow, Nell had hurried across to converse with Mr. Pettifer on more than one occasion. Her visits had occurred on a number of nights, establishing a firm friendship between Mr. Pettifer and herself, even if his boasted frankness occasionally tested her patience. Her presence was still met with distrust by Nutmeg, who always sarcastically addressed her as “redheaded snippet.” In an effort to cure him of this behavior, Mr. Pettifer would leap up in excitement each time he spotted Nell approaching, shouting,
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0028 }

“Bless my soul, there is that charming young lady once more,” or a remark of an identical complimentary nature. Nutmeg, however, perceived the ruse and held it in contempt. Nell was destined to remain ignorant of the numerous flatteries Mr. Pettifer bestowed upon her in her absence. He undoubtedly refrained from offering her a single one in her presence.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0029 }

“Well, I guess you have been out among the trees gathering a store of rods for the next day?” he said to welcome her while Nell walked up the stairs to the porch.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0030 }

“No, indeed,” Nell replied with indignation. Because she constantly took matters with such earnestness, she made a wonderful target to tease. “There will never be a switch present in my school, Mr. Pettifer. Naturally, a pointer will be necessary for me to possess, yet I will employ it solely for pointing.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0031 }

“So you intend to use the strap on them in place of that? Well, I am not certain, yet you might be correct. Although a switch causes a sharper pain initially, there is no denying that the strap leaves a lingering ache.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0032 }

“I will use nothing like that. It is not my intention to whip those I teach.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0033 }

“Bless my soul,” Mr. Pettifer cried out, truly amazed, “in what way do you plan to maintain discipline then?”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0034 }

“My rule will be one of affection, Mr. Pettifer.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0035 }

“It isn't right,” Mr. Pettifer said, “not right whatsoever, Nell. ‘Spare the rod and spoil the child.’ Back when I attended school, the master flogged me routinely each day on the grounds that if I was not causing trouble at that moment, I was planning it.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0036 }

“Since the time you attended school, Mr. Pettifer, techniques have evolved.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0037 }

“Yet mankind's essence remains unchanged. Pay attention to what I say, you will not succeed in controlling the youth if you do not have a punishment prepared for them. It cannot be done.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0038 }

“Well, I’m going to try my way first,” declared Nell, whose will was quite resolute and who tended to hold on extremely firmly to her ideas.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0039 }

“I suppose you possess a fair amount of obstinacy,” Mr. Pettifer expressed. “Oh well, time will tell. On some future occasion when your temper is ignited . . . and individuals possessing your shade of hair have a strong tendency to lose their tempers . . . you will cast aside all your delicate ideas and thrash a few of them. In any case, your age makes you unsuitable for teaching . . . much too youthful and immature.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0040 }

On the whole, a somewhat gloomy state of mind accompanied Nell as she retired for the night. Her sleep was fitful, and her appearance at the following morning's breakfast was so wan and mournful that Thirza felt frightened and demanded that she drink a cup of burning ginger tea. Nell drank it slowly and without complaint, even though she failed to see how ginger tea could help. If it had been a magical potion capable of bestowing maturity and wisdom, Nell would have gulped down a quart without hesitation.
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0041 }

“Thirza, suppose I do not succeed!”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0042 }

“You’re unlikely to suffer total failure during a single day, and many additional days lie ahead,” Thirza remarked. “Your problem, Nell, stems from your expectation that you will instruct those kids in every subject and correct every one of their flaws immediately, and should that prove impossible, you will view yourself as a failure.”
{: #nw-v02-c04-p0043 }
